_meta.what: Last ACCEPTED byte sizes for append-only docs, read by handoff-preflight.py.
why: decisions.md is an append-only architectural log that is legitimately large and is
already ~4x any sane absolute cap. Gating it on an absolute number would block every
/handoff until someone swept. It is gated on GROWTH SINCE THIS RECORDED SIZE instead,
which is change-keyed: a normal handoff appending a decision or two passes; an unswept
accumulation past the growth budget trips it.
An ABSENT or corrupt file here does NOT mean 'fine' — handoff-preflight.py falls back
to an absolute cap that decisions.md already exceeds, so it fails CLOSED.
how_to_update: THEN record the post-sweep size here. Do NOT raise this number merely to silence the
gate: it records a size that was ACCEPTED after a sweep, not merely the current one.
last_sweep: 2026-08-08: decisions.md 1,129,290 -> 1,047,198. 22 legacy-format entries moved VERBATIM to
memory/decisions-archive.md. This number is LOWER than the previous baseline (1,053,789), so it
is a recorded GAIN, not a silenced gate — the budget now measures growth from the smaller size.
SELECTION RULE, worth reusing: entries were chosen by CITATION, not by age. An entry qualified
only if it sat in the legacy '## <date> — [TAG] D<N>:' heading region AND no live doc cited its
D-number (CLAUDE.md, LEDGER, STOP-CATALOGUE, parking, goals, specs/, plans/, scripts/). 116
legacy entries were KEPT because they ARE cited live — D293, D294, D276, D336, D220 among them.
'Old' is NOT 'non-load-bearing': a blanket age sweep would have archived live binding rules.
⚠ Preserve CRLF when rewriting this file's targets. Python's default text mode converts every
CRLF to LF, which would have produced a 7,679-line spurious diff. Caught only because the
script's byte count disagreed with the gate's by exactly the line count.

2026-08-14 (Sweep 2): decisions.md 923,768 -> 696,696 (270 -> 195 entries, 75 moved). Same citation selection rule, now scripted at .claude/scripts/sweep-decisions.py (re-runnable -- it recomputes the live-doc citation scan at run time rather than reusing a cached list). Two fixes found before this sweep ran, both worth keeping in the script for next time:

(1) RANGE-CITATION BLIND SPOT -- a plain 'D<digits>' substring match misses entries covered by a range citation like 'D579-D590' or 'D323-D333' (29 such ranges exist across goals.md, STOP-CATALOGUE.md, and specs/); the script now expands every range to its full inclusive set before diffing. Without this fix, ~10 entries genuinely covered by a live citation would have been wrongly swept.

(2) UNCOMMITTED IN-FLIGHT ENTRIES -- the script excludes any D-number not yet present in 'git show HEAD:.claude/decisions.md', so a decision written earlier the same session (uncited only because it hasn't had time to be cited yet) is never swept.

16 kept entries reference a swept D-number internally (e.g. D612 mentions D604/D607/D611) -- not a problem, the archived entry keeps its number and stays grep-able across both files, but logged rather than left silent, per D101 (never silently drop a reference).

2026-08-14 (Phase 2 compression, same day as Sweep 2): decisions.md 696,696 -> 432,679 bytes (195 entries, unchanged -- no entries removed this pass, only compressed in place). Every remaining entry was a 4-9KB full incident narrative despite CLAUDE.md already describing this doc as 'compressed'; rewrote each body down to ~3-8 tight lines keeping the ruling, the one-line why, and every concrete fact (numbers, file:line, commit hashes, function/attribute names, dates, D-cross-references, status) -- cut only the investigation narrative. Full pre-compression text remains permanently recoverable via git history (this file was fully committed before the rewrite). Done via 11 parallel size-balanced batches (~70KB each); every batch's D-number set was verified byte-for-byte against the source before reassembly (one batch, D575-D587, silently dropped 3 entries on its first pass -- caught by the mechanical count check, not by trusting the agent's own summary, and redone correctly on retry).

2026-08-14 (/adversarial-council review, 6 personas): tested whether more entries could safely be archived on the grounds of 'redundant with their citing spec'. 4/6 personas independently concluded NO -- tested against real entries (not just discussed), a redundancy-with-spec test targets the WRONG entries (single-citation entries usually hold irreplaceable forensic detail a spec deliberately doesn't restate -- 65 entries are cited by a spec that explicitly says 'full detail lives in decisions.md, do not duplicate here'). Even a perfect-execution best case of such a mechanism wouldn't reach the 262,144-byte fallback cap anyway (computed ceiling ~347KB). Real bugs found and fixed instead: sweep-decisions.py's citation scope was missing architecture.md/dev-setup.md and didn't exclude .claude/worktrees/ (both closed); the archive mixes two incompatible heading formats ('## D<N>' and '**D<N>') and had no index, so ~82% of it was invisible to any tool that only recognised one format -- fixed with .claude/scripts/build-archive-index.py (idempotent, re-run after every future sweep). D101 was flagged as 'missing an entry body' -- investigated and it's not a bug: it was never logged as a discrete decisions.md entry, the rule is stated in full inline in .claude/CLAUDE.md's own table, nothing was lost.

2026-08-14 (Phase 2b, second compression pass): decisions.md 432,679 -> 427,093 bytes. Targeted the 99 entries still over 2KB after Phase 2's first pass; result was a modest ~1.3% further reduction, not the larger gain initially estimated -- most of those entries turned out to already be dense forensic records (root causes, exact figures, rejected alternatives, method lessons) with little safe room left to cut without violating the explicit keep-every-fact instruction. Several batch agents correctly reported hitting that floor rather than forcing artificial cuts. This confirms the council's finding: compression has a real but limited ceiling on already-compressed content, and the honest next lever (if ever needed) is citation-based archiving of individual entries as they age out of relevance, not further blanket compression.

_meta.sweep_owed: NONE in practice. The 262,144-byte fallback cap is not the real gate -- check_decisions_size() is growth-keyed (baseline + 65,536-byte budget) and the file passes cleanly today; the absolute cap only applies when no baseline is recorded (handoff-preflight.py:613-627). decisions.md is also not auto-loaded into any session (grep confirms no SessionStart hook or script reads its content, only its size), so its byte count costs zero context per session. Chasing the 262KB number further is not a real requirement -- see the 2026-08-14 council entry above. If growth ever does trip the gate, re-run sweep-decisions.py; that mechanism alone is safe and sufficient.
